To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the toxicity of oil to plants is dependent on the oil’s constituents, amount, environmental conditions, and plant species.
oils vary in their toxicity and the higher the concentration of certain constituents, the more severe the effects on plants.
oils reduce transpiration rate and photosynthesis, and increase respiration rate.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (i) the effect of oils and their constituents on the physiology of plants, (ii) the effect of oil contamination on the yield of crops, (iii) the effect of the oils and their constituents in the soil on the yield of plants grown in the soil, and (iv) the effect of plant extracts on the toxicity of oils to plants.
the effects of oils and oil constituents on plant processes and the mechanisms of their action.
the effects of oils on plant growth and metabolism, the mechanisms by which these effects occur, and the factors which modify the toxicity of oils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

oil is toxic to plants, but the extent and severity of its effect depends on the oil and plant species involved, the environmental conditions, the amount of oil, the time of contact with the plant, etc.
the effects of oil on plants are very complex, and that the results of experiments are often difficult to explain.
oils are phytotoxic to all plant species, and that this phytotoxicity depends on a variety of factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oils are toxic to all plants, though the severity of the damage varies greatly.

the oil from the leaves of the oil palm (Elaeis guineensis Jacq) is more toxic to the plant than is the fruit mesocarp oil, and that the oil from young leaves is more toxic than that from older leaves.
oils can have many adverse effects on plants, but the severity of the effects varies considerably, and depends on a number of factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
oils can have a range of effects, and that these effects can vary according to the type of oil, the amount of oil and the environmental conditions.
the oil from a single plant can vary greatly in composition and toxicity depending on environmental and genetic factors.
the effects of oils on the plant are not always predictable.
